sentences.text: Heard Mr. K. Bhuyan, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr.
R.R. Kaushik, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor representing the State of Assam.
This is an application under Section 439 of the CrPC in respect of Jalukbari P.S. Case No.295/2023 registered under Sections 120- B/468/471/420/384/34 of the IPC.
Page No.# 2/2
The informant Jayanta Sarmah claimed to be the owner of 2 Bighas of land.

He has alleged that 4 persons, namely- Nilakhi Devi, Mukulita Sarmah Kakoti, Indranil Das Gupta,
Mukkardar Khan @ Kuku and the present petitioner have illegally occupied a portion of land and Mukkader Khan @ Kuku vs The State Of Assam on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166064561/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner submits that his wife had purchased 4 Kathas of land from Indranil Das Gupta.
According to the petitioner, deal was done after perusal of land records.
A copy of the land records is also available with the records.
Mr. Kaushik submits that the present petitioner is a habitual offender.
He is regularly involved in such type of offences.
I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsels of both sides.
It is clear from the available records that there is a genuine civil dispute between the parties.
Therefore, the petitioner does not deserve to be detained in custody.
His bail application is allowed.

It is hereby directed that the petitioner Mukkader Khan @ Kuku shall be released on a bail bond of Rs.25,000/- with a surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Kamrup(M), Guwahati.
The bail application stands disposed of.
Return the case diary.
